comparison: Both address RTN4RL2 expression claims (C2, C3). OpenEval finds the RNAscope ISH data with KO controls sufficient for SUPPORTED evaluation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting quantitative assessment of expression levels rather than just visual data, undermining confidence despite the negative controls.

Perfect agreement on claims C4-C5 regarding SGN soma counts. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this finding when discussing other results, and OpenEval notes the quantitative analysis at multiple timepoints establishes no gross cellular loss.

Both address ribbon size claims (C6, C7). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on quantitative immunofluorescence across multiple cochlear regions. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to methodological concerns about measuring orphan ribbons vs. orphan PSDs directly, noting critical quantification was provided only in rebuttal, not manuscript.

Both address PSD size claims (C8, C9). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with acknowledged limitation about immunolabeling sensitivity. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, grouping these claims with C6-C7 and C10, raising methodological concerns about the approach to quantifying orphan PSDs versus ribbons.

OpenEval addresses orphan PSDs (C10, C44) as SUPPORTED, linking immunolabeling to SBEM data. Peer review groups C10 with C6-C9 in UNCERTAIN evaluation, identifying critical logical inconsistency: unchanged ribbon counts with additional orphan PSDs but no increase in SGN soma creates unresolved discrepancy.

Both address C44 (efferent synapse exclusion). OpenEval includes this with C10 as SUPPORTED evidence for orphan PSD interpretation. Peer review treats C44 alone as SUPPORTED methodological control, accepting it distinguishes orphan PSDs from efferent synapses without challenge.

Both address GluA2/3 receptor claims (C12-C15). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on immunolabeling, quantification, and RNAscope data. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, identifying temporal mismatch (GluA2/3 labeling at 1-1.5 months vs. Gria2 RNAscope at P4) and lack of quantification for RNA expression, weakening the maintained-mRNA-despite-reduced-protein conclusion.

Perfect claim overlap (C16-C19) on SBEM reconstruction of non-synaptic neurites. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on detailed reconstruction and statistical analysis. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to logical inconsistency: unchanged ribbon counts plus orphan PSDs should require more SGNs, but SGN soma counts are unchanged—this discrepancy undermines interpretation.

Perfect agreement on electrophysiology claims (C20-C23). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes comprehensive patch-clamp data with appropriate statistics showing selective Vhalf effect. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the depolarized shift in CaV1.3 activation as a key finding indicating altered presynaptic functionality.

Perfect agreement on Ca2+ imaging claims (C24-C27). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes consistency between whole-cell and single AZ measurements plus immunolabeling controls. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as supporting the depolarized shift and proper presynaptic component localization.

Both address ABR/hearing impairment (C28-C30, with peer also including C31). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes statistical significance and dose-dependent effect in heterozygotes. Peer reviewers across all three reviews accept the hearing impairment phenotype as solid, well-supported finding using multiple advanced techniques.

Both address integrative conclusions (C31, C37 in OpenEval; C35, C37, C39 in peer review). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for C31/C37 as convergence of multiple findings. Peer review rates SUPPORTED for mechanistic interpretations including C35 (BAI1 interaction speculation) and C39 (reduced Ca2+ influx mechanism), accepting these as reasonable interpretations.

Partial overlap on C31 (synaptopathy conclusion). OpenEval groups C31 with C37 as SUPPORTED integrative conclusion from converging evidence. Peer review includes C31 with C28-C30 in SUPPORTED evaluation of hearing impairment and synaptic dysfunction, treating it as accepted interpretation.

Both address C35 (RTN4RL2-BAI1 interaction hypothesis). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculation based on phenotypic similarities and known interactions but lacking direct experimental evidence in cochlea. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, accepting this as reasonable mechanistic interpretation within broader context of synaptic disruption findings.

Both address C39 (reduced Ca2+ influx mechanism). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED (C38-C41), finding the mechanistic logic sound with supporting citations. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, explicitly acknowledging the depolarized shift leads to impaired neurotransmitter release and compromised synaptic transmission.

OpenEval addresses C42-C43 (comparison to GluA3 KO phenotype) as SUPPORTED based on citations and lack of GluA4 compensation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these comparative claims.

OpenEval addresses C45-C49 (failed pruning vs. noise-induced synaptopathy distinction) as UNCERTAIN—preserved synapse counts rule out noise damage, but failed pruning mechanism remains speculative without developmental studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval addresses C36 (bidirectional trans-synaptic signaling context) as SUPPORTED based on appropriate citations. This contextual claim about IHC-SGN synapse biology has no corresponding peer review evaluation.

OpenEval addresses C50-C54 (literature context on RTN4R family and BAI1 interactions) as SUPPORTED background claims appropriately cited. These contextual claims for future mechanistic studies have no corresponding peer review evaluation.

OpenEval addresses C1, C11, C55-C68 (established background knowledge) as SUPPORTED, appropriately cited context. These 16 background claims providing essential context are not specifically evaluated in peer review results.
